title: Gravity and Space
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Gravity and Space Worksheets (Weight = Mass × g, Light Years, Seasons)
standard_text: Gravity force, weight = mass × gravitational field strength (g), on Earth g = 10 N/kg, different on other planets and stars; gravity forces between Earth and Moon, and between Earth and Sun (qualitative only); our Sun as a star, other stars in our galaxy, other galaxies; the seasons and the Earth's tilt, day length at different times of year, in different hemispheres; the light year as a unit of astronomical distance.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on gravity and space: mass and weight, weight = mass × g, gravity on other planets, orbits, stars and galaxies, light years and the seasons. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: On Earth g ≈ 10 N/kg; mass stays the same everywhere.
body_html:
How to think about it

Gravity pulls masses together; weight is the force of gravity on a mass.

  • weight (N) = mass (kg) × g (N/kg). On Earth g ≈ 10 N/kg; on the Moon about 1.6 N/kg. Mass stays the same.
  • Gravity keeps the Moon and planets in orbit. Stars are grouped into galaxies; distances are measured in light years.
  • Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis, not by its distance from the Sun.
Example

50 kg on Earth (10 N/kg). Weight?

50 × 10

Answer: 500 N

Example

Same 50 kg on the Moon (1.6 N/kg)?

50 × 1.6

Answer: 80 N

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mass and weight.
  • Thinking there is no gravity in space.
  • Thinking summer happens because the Earth is closer to the Sun.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter, in kilograms, and is the same everywhere. Weight is the force of gravity on it, in newtons, and depends on where you are.
Multiply the mass by the gravitational field strength: weight = mass × g. On Earth, g is about 10 N/kg.
The Earth's axis is tilted. When the northern hemisphere tilts towards the Sun it has summer: longer days and the Sun higher in the sky.
